basis_statement: VCF Automation publishes no specification in the vmware/vcf-api-specs repository. docs/contract.json was therefore transcribed from the rendered VCF Automation xAPIs reference pages on developer.broadcom.com. Every page read is listed below with the operation it documents and the date it was fetched. Pages that were read and then not used are listed too, so the record shows what was surveyed and not only what was kept.
fetched_with: HTTP fetch of the rendered reference pages

sources.title: Create Policy 1 | VM Apps Org - Policies | VCF Automation API
sources.used_for: Primary source for the operation. Summary 'Creates a new policy, updates an existing policy, or trigger a policy dry-run.'; the complete Policy request body property list with types, formats, required flags, descriptions and the maxLength 1024 / maxLength 2000 / SOFT|HARD constraints; id typed string format uuid and marked optional; query parameters dryRun and validationOnly; response statuses 200 OK, 201 Created, 202 Accepted, 400 Bad Request, 401 Unauthorized, 403 Forbidden, each described as 'Operation doesn't return any data structure'; bearerAuth security; the curl example showing Authorization and Content-Type as the only request headers.

sources.title: Create Policy 1 | VM Apps Org - Catalog | VCF Automation API
sources.operation: upsertPolicy - POST /policy/api/policies (second portal path for the same operation)
sources.used_for: Independent cross-check of the request body property list and status codes. It agreed on every property, on the SOFT/HARD enum and default HARD, and on the status set. It disagreed on the type of the dryRun query parameter, rendering it boolean where the primary page rendered it string; that disagreement is why docs/contract.json records dryRun without pinning a type.

sources.title: Get Policy 1 | VM Apps Org - Policies | VCF Automation API
sources.used_for: Path and required path parameter id; the optional computeStats query parameter; response statuses 200, 401, 403, 404; and the full Policy response property list, including the statistics object carrying enforcedCount, notEnforcedCount and conflictCount. This is the only one of the two operations that documents a response body, which is why the stored policy is read back through it.

sources.title: VCF Automation API Reference Guide Operations Index
sources.operation: index of every operation in the VCF Automation API
sources.used_for: Confirmed that POST /policy/api/policies and GET /policy/api/policies/{id} are the operation set for a policy upsert, and that the API's request/task resources (/deployment/api/requests/{requestId} and friends) live under /deployment/api only. No request, task or job resource is documented under /policy/api, which is the evidence behind the contract's treatment of a 202 from upsertPolicy as unresolvable.

sources.title: VCF Automation API | VM Apps Org - Policies
sources.used_for: API title 'VCF Automation API', description 'A multi-cloud API for Cloud Automation Services', and the version selector listing 9.1 (Latest) and 9.0.

sources.title: VCF Automation API | VM Apps Org - Catalog
sources.used_for: Corroborated the API title, description and 9.1/9.0 version listing, and documented the OData-like collection query parameters ($orderby, $top, $skip, page, size). None of those apply to the two operations in this contract.

sources.title: Request Catalog Item Instances | VM Apps Org - Catalog
sources.used_for: Surveyed as a candidate mutating operation. Its CatalogItemRequest body (bulkRequestCount, deploymentName, inputs, projectId, reason, version) carries no client-choosable identity, so redelivering it creates another deployment. It was rejected for that reason and the upsert was used instead.

sources.title: VCF Automation and All Apps API - Broadcom TechDocs
sources.operation: product documentation - checked for request header conventions
sources.used_for: Read to check whether VCF Automation requires a versioned media type such as application/json;version=9.1.0. The page documents only the /provider and /automation console URLs and names no request header, so no versioned Accept header was added to the contract. Recorded as negative evidence for why the contract's header set is as small as it is.
